checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Poster, story and reel all display exactly '24 October 2027'
must.why: The story (image 3) and poster (image 4) read '24 October 2027'. The reel shows it at 1 s, 4 s and 7 s. By 9.5 s the zoom has pushed all the text out of frame.

must.item: Old date '17 October 2027' absent from both images and every reel frame
must.why: No '17' appears in the revised images or in any of the four sampled reel frames. I can't check the frames between those four.

must.item: All three retain 'Rooftop Jazz', '7 PM', 'Atlas Roof', 'Free entry' unaltered
must.why: On the poster, 'Rooftop' is cut off at the top edge, so the title is not fully shown. The story image keeps all the text. In the reel the text is cropped by the zoom and gone by 9.5 s.

must.item: Revised assets preserve original cream-and-burgundy design, imagery and layouts
must.why: The palette, sax player, skyline, frame and layout all match the originals. The poster's crop matches the original poster's crop.

must.item: Pack has two separate images and one 10-second reel in requested aspect ratios
must.why: The story is 9:16 (360x640), the poster is 4:5 (512x640) and the reel is 9:16 (480x864) at 10 s. The reel has sound.

exact_text.read_as: Story and reel opening: 'Rooftop JAZZ', complete. Poster: 'Rooftop' is clipped at the top, leaving only the lower half of the letters.

faults.what: The 4:5 poster crops the title: 'Rooftop' is cut off at the top edge. It is a crop of the story image, not a re-laid-out poster.
The reel zooms in so far that the title and date are cropped. By 9.5 s only the sax player is on screen and no text is visible.
The reel's frame is cropped and zoomed, so the burgundy border and the layout are lost.
The story image and reel show slight softness and AI artefacts in the text rendering, such as the sax and the date digits.

summary: The date is correctly changed to 24 October 2027 on all three pieces and the old date is gone, but the poster crops the 'Rooftop' title and the reel zooms so far that the text leaves the frame by the end.
